content: The Consolidated HIV Strategic Information Guidelines: Driving Impact Through Programme Monitoring and Management was published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in April 2020. This document provides comprehensive guidance on the use of strategic information to enhance the impact of HIV programs through effective monitoring and management. It is available in both electronic and print formats, with respective ISBNs 978-92-4-000073-5 and 978-92-4-000074-2. The document includes acknowledgments of the contributions made by various working groups, technical experts, and organizations. These groups include the Core Working Group, chaired by David Lowrance (WHO, Switzerland) and co-chaired by Virginia Loo (WHO consultant, USA), as well as numerous other members representing global health organizations, academic institutions, and national health ministries. The guidelines also recognize the efforts of technical working groups focused on specific areas such as condom use, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), HIV testing and linkage, antiretroviral treatment and viral load monitoring, HIV drug resistance, ART toxicity, TB/HIV integration, prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT), and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Each working group is composed of experts from diverse backgrounds, including representatives from WHO, UNAIDS, the Global Fund, CDC, USAID, UNICEF, and other international and national health organizations. These groups have contributed to the development of evidence-based recommendations and strategies to address key challenges in HIV prevention, treatment, and care. The guidelines emphasize the importance of disaggregated data, electronic health information systems, and routine data reviews to inform programmatic decisions and improve outcomes. They also highlight the need for evaluation and operational research to ensure the effectiveness and sustainability of HIV interventions. The document serves as a critical resource for policymakers, program managers, and healthcare providers working to combat the global HIV epidemic.
